# Introduction

The `PIFDataModel` package provides standardized schemas to validate and structure biological data, ensuring consistency and interoperability across applications. This vignette details the schemas available in the package, their purpose, and how to utilize them effectively.

# Schema Categories

The table below lists the schemas available in the `PIFDataModel` package:

| **Category**      | **Name**                        | **Description**                                       | **Link**                                               |
|--------------------|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Bacteria**       | Count                          | Schema for bacteria count information                 | [View](./schemas/bacteria_count_schema.json)               |
|                    | General                        | Schema for general information about bacteria         | [View](./schemas/bacteria_schema.json)                     |
|                    | Prevalence                     | Schema for bacteria prevalence                        | [View](./schemas/bacteria_prevalence_schema.json)          |
|                    | Results                        | Schema for results related to bacteria analysis       | [View](./schemas/bacteria_general_results_schema.json)             |
|                    | Tree                           | Schema for hierarchical tree structure of bacteria    | [View](./schemas/bacteria_tree_schema.json)                |


# Examples

Below are examples of how to load and use schemas in R:

## Loading the `PIFDataModel` Package

```r
# Load the PIFDataModel package
library(PIFDataModel)
```

## Accessing the Bacteria Count Schema

```{r}
# Load the JSON schema
bacteria_schema <- jsonlite::read_json("../inst/schemas/bacteria_count_schema.json")

# Print the schema
print(bacteria_schema)
```

### Example Output

Here is a sample of the `bacteria_count_schema.json`:

<details>
<summary>Bacteria Count Schema</summary>
<pre>
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "title": "Bacteria Count Schema",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "species": {"type": "string"},
    "count": {"type": "integer"},
    "location": {"type": "string"},
    "date": {"type": "string", "format": "date"}
  },
  "required": ["species", "count", "location", "date"]
}
</pre>
</details>
